title: Check declared build-input sets against the real compiled-in inputs
summary: Root cause: a declared list (CI cache globs, input_files, BUILD_PATHS, ontology terms) is checked for shape but never against the source it summarizes, so errors surface only at the final verdict. Add a code check that derives the athena binary's real input set (every include_str!/include_bytes! target under crates/ plus BUILD_PATHS) and fails if the ci.yml athena-bin hashFiles globs or xtask input_files miss any. Audience: Athena maintainers and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: Fix the shared cause: declared lists never checked against their real source.
Enforced by a test, not prose.
Test plus fmt, clippy and cargo test criteria.
Negative fixture test checks the failure happening.
One focused check; ontology and pipeline changes excluded.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (BUILD_PATHS at line 20 is the repo's definition of build inputs), crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs and briefs.rs (include_str! of prompts and docs/system-facts.md), and grep of include_str! across crates/*/src. Entry point is a new test in crates/athena-core (cargo test), run before verification; it reads files from the workspace root, scans sources for include_str!/include_bytes! targets, resolves them relative to the source file, and compares with BUILD_PATHS and the hashFiles globs parsed from .github/workflows/ci.yml. No new record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not affected; the allow-list is untouched. The property is measured directly: the real include set versus the declared globs, not a stand-in.

Prior job 20261031-172040-kq9v: its finding (athena-bin key omitted prompts and docs/system-facts.md) already appears fixed in the repo's ci.yml (globs crates/**, xtask/**, docs/system-facts.md). This change keeps that work as is and adds the mechanism the finding's minor item asked for, so the hand-kept list cannot drift again. The stamp-on-non-CI-build, restored build-commit and dirty-tree findings are not addressed here; they are minor, local, and listed out of scope.

Prior job 20261017-173508-0wtc (ontology term contradicts BRIEF.md): addressed at the class level only through the shared mechanism of checking a declared list against its governing source; the ontology content itself is left as is and not touched here. Prior job 20261025-214509-y179 (speed target not met, no baseline): its code changes (secrets.rs memo, checks.rs poll schedule) are kept untouched; the measure-first stage is out of scope because it is a pipeline change needing its own job.
The check parses hashFiles patterns with a simple glob match (prefix/** and exact file names), enough for the current ci.yml; a pattern form it cannot parse fails loudly rather than passing.

acceptance_criteria.text: The change description (CHANGELOG.md entry) names the root cause: declared input lists were checked for structure but not against the real compiled-in inputs, citing jobs 20261031-172040-kq9v, 20261017-173508-0wtc and 20261025-214509-y179 and saying how each prior result is addressed or why it is out of scope.

A new test under crates/athena-core derives the input set from every include_str!/include_bytes! target under crates/*/src plus BUILD_PATHS, and asserts each is covered by the athena-bin hashFiles globs in .github/workflows/ci.yml (all jobs) and by BUILD_PATHS; it reads ci.yml rather than a copy.

Negative test: run `cargo test -p athena-core` on in-memory fixtures where a glob list omits a prompt .md file or docs/system-facts.md; the check returns a failure naming the missing path. The same fixtures with the full list pass. The test fails against the pre-fix key from job kq9v (only *.rs and Cargo.toml globs).
Run `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass on the real repository, so the current ci.yml satisfies the new check.
The check is a refusal rule over repository files, not over readings; no replay of past readings is affected (expected 0% of newly refused readings).

out_of_scope: Changing docs/ontology.toml, crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs or any study (job 0wtc work stays dropped/unchanged)
Changing crates/athena-gate/src/secrets.rs, crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs or the test-speed goal (job y179 work kept as is)
Changing xtask/src/main.rs, xtask/tests/policy.rs or the setup.sh stamp and dirty-tree behavior (job kq9v work kept as is)
A measure-first stage for speed-target jobs
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, tool pins or action SHAs
departures: Reading is a judgment call among three loosely related causes; acceptance is lowered slightly.
urgent_reason: Cuts redo-work: the same declared-versus-real mismatch has caused three rejected jobs (0wtc, y179, kq9v) caught only at the final verdict.
hard_reason: Adds a check that can fail the repository tests and gates what CI treats as the binary's input set, so a mistake is costly.
